1 Purpose and decision framework

This report tests whether the current WGCNA network is sensitive to retaining the 5,000, 10,000, or 15,000 most variable genes. It reconstructs each network from the same 30 individual RNA-seq libraries while keeping the correlation method, network type, module-detection settings, and planned site contrasts fixed. The soft-thresholding power is re-evaluated separately for each gene set because the connectivity distribution changes when additional genes enter the network.

The comparison is not designed to select the network with the highest scale-free-topology fit alone. The final gene set should balance network connectivity, module assignment, preservation of modules across nested gene sets, site-stratified resampling stability, and computational reproducibility. Annotation coverage is a secondary practical criterion. Site-contrast significance, DEG overlap, enrichment yield, and chemistry are downstream sensitivity results and cannot determine network parameters. Gene-set preservation in this report is a feature-selection sensitivity analysis and does not replace the site-stratified resampling analysis required to evaluate module robustness.

4 2. Load and rank the expression matrix

Genes are ranked once by variance across all 30 VST libraries. The 5,000-, 10,000-, and 15,000-gene networks are therefore nested and differ only by the number of lower-ranked genes admitted to the network. Site labels are not used for feature selection.

Expression input and sensitivity-design summary.

5 3. Reconstruct the networks

Each network uses the same signed biweight-midcorrelation design. The soft-thresholding power is selected independently using the current Step 02 rule: the lowest tested power reaching the target is retained; when the target is not reached, the power with the highest available fit is used. Diagnostics at power 12 are also retained so that the effect of adding genes can be compared at a common power.

7 5. Preservation of modules across nested gene sets

Reference modules are matched to modules in the larger network after restricting both assignments to their shared genes. Jaccard similarity measures overlap in gene membership. Eigengene-profile correlation measures whether the matched modules retain the same dominant expression pattern across the 30 libraries; its absolute value is reported because eigengene signs are arbitrary. The high/moderate/low classes are transparent heuristics for screening and are not formal WGCNA preservation statistics.

8 6. Preservation of planned site-contrast signals

The three planned contrasts are fitted separately within each reconstructed network using the individual-library module eigengenes. Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied across all module-by-contrast tests within each network. Because module labels and eigengene signs are arbitrary across networks, direct cross-network effect comparisons are made only for the best-matched modules and the test-network effect is aligned to the sign of the eigengene-profile correlation.

10 8. Structural power sensitivity for the 10,000-gene candidate

The 10,000-gene candidate is reconstructed at powers 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20 with every other network setting fixed. Selection uses connectivity, module assignment, adjacent-power preservation, and site-stratified resampling only. Site contrasts, DEG overlap, enrichment yield, and chemistry are not available to the power-selection rule.

14.1 Selected network for the downstream exploratory rerun

The 10,000-gene universe is selected as the smallest expanded network that retains much of the 5,000-gene structure without the greater fragmentation and weaker incremental preservation of the 15,000-gene expansion. Its improved annotation coverage is a secondary practical benefit. DEG recovery, site significance, enrichment yield, and chemistry do not enter this decision.

14.2 Reading the comparison

None of the tested gene sets reached the prespecified scale-free-topology target. The final network should therefore not be described as scale-free, and gene-set selection should rely on the combined diagnostics rather than on this statistic alone.

The strongest overall cross-size module preservation occurred for the 5,000 to 10,000 comparison (median Jaccard = 0.615; median absolute eigengene correlation = 0.991).

The 10,000-gene universe is selected from structural evidence: cross-universe preservation, site-stratified resampling stability, connectivity, assignment, and module-size behaviour. Annotation coverage is secondary. Site-contrast significance, DEG recovery, enrichment yield, and chemistry were excluded from selection. Within the 10,000-gene universe, power 14 is the lowest candidate meeting the declared connectivity, scale-free-fit-deficit, and resampling-stability criteria. Step 08 consumes this explicit final-network handoff.
